body.statement: There is a universal \(L<\infty\) such that for every admissible sequence, \[\Pr_{G_n}\!\left\{\|B_{G_n}P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\right\}\longrightarrow1.\]
body.justification: This is the graph-certificate synthesis needed by the inherited log-tuned two-arm design; its genuinely new input is exactly Open-ended Question 1 in the dense range.
body.gap: The Kandiros--Harshaw--S\'{a}vje bracket does not provide this Boolean operator event, and the archived version-one run leaves its dense signed four-root input unresolved.
body.consumer: Theorem 3 converts this event into the \(r_{\log}(n,d_n)\) worst-case MSE upper bound.

obligation.what_is_open:
The dense-range implication needed to extend the proved sparse Boolean
operator estimate to every \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) remains open.
obligation.obstruction:
The sparse theorem covers every stage with \(d_n\le n^{2/5}\).  At a dense
stage, the fourth-trace identity reduces the desired probability to the
unresolved signed four-root moment.  Using the unproved OEQ as a premise
would make the limit law of the graph certificate an assumption rather
than a derived conclusion.
obligation.attempted:
The matrix was centered by its exact off-diagonal mean, giving
\[
B_{G_n}P_n=X_{G_n}P_n+(1-p_{n,d_n})P_n.
\]
The repeated-index contributions to the fourth trace were bounded by
\(Cnd_n^4\), and the four-distinct contribution was reduced exactly to
\(n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3)\mu_{\mathrm{cyc}}\).  Frobenius, maximum-row, and
termwise collision bounds all lose a power in the dense range.
obligation.partial_result:
Theorem~\(\mathrm{thm{:}sparse\mbox{-}boolean\mbox{-}operator}\) proves the
claimed event for every stage with \(d_n\le n^{2/5}\).  If the signed OEQ
bound is established, the preceding fourth-moment reduction proves the
same event on every stage with \(d_n\ge n^{2/5}\), and the two cases splice
without any fixed-degree interchange.
